title: 06 rejects an unregistered $function that no clause forbids; a conforming compiler fails it
detail: VERIFIED. Fixture is `//! reject $fixture_vpi_function` on `analog I(p,n) <+ $fixture_vpi_function(V(p,n));`. Stripped docs/VAMS-LRM/ch11-vpi.html has 0 occurrences of 'shall be an error', 'illegal', 'is an error', 'not permitted', 'must not', 'may not' -- Clause 11 states no error rule at all. 2.8.3 makes `$name` grammatical and assigns its meaning to simulator functionality; 12.32's compiletf hands refusal to the registered application. The directory already says so: 05_system_task_call_object.va:11-12 reads 'An earlier revision of this fixture demanded a rejection -- the LRM does not require one', and 05:29-31 compiles and RUNS the identical construct. The split is pure VerA DCE: src/backend/codegen.zig:2698 `self.abort("VerA does not implement `{s}` (ch9); a substitute value would corrupt the model")` only fires when the call's value is rendered, true for a contribution RHS and false for 05's bare statement. The `//! reject` substring is that raw abort string -- not a diag code, no entry in src/diag_code.zig. E0801 'unsupported system function' exists but src/ir/lower.zig:2444 isRejectedSysFunc lists only the 9.13 random/dist family and 9.21 $table_model, so it never fires here. `//! xfail` is the wrong escape: xfail means the LRM demands a diagnostic VerA does not emit; this is VerA emitting one the LRM does not demand.
expected: Rewrite on the 05/08 pattern as a runnable fixture. Header: `//! lrm 11.6.16`, `//! lrm 2.8.3`, `//! bias V(p) = 1.5, V(n) = 0.25`. Body calls `$fixture_vpi_function` in STATEMENT position (which 05 proves VerA accepts) with `seq = 1; $fixture_vpi_function(V(p,n)); seq = seq + 2;` then `CHECKI("the block continues past an unregistered system call", seq, 3)` and `CHECKX("and the probe is unchanged by it", V(p,n), 1.25)` (1.5 - 0.25, both dyadic). Delete 06_system_function_call_object.expected-error.txt (covered by ch11-05). If instead the file is deleted outright, move the s11-6-16 COVERAGE row onto 18/19.

title: 20 is the same unbacked rejection as 06, one identifier apart, and it is why the 19/20 atomic pair encodes 'task legal, function illegal'
detail: VERIFIED identical construction: `//! reject $fixture_vpi_function_object` on `analog I(p,n) <+ $fixture_vpi_function_object(V(p,n));`. Same raw-abort-string reject, same absent rule. Leaving it draws a task/function distinction no clause draws, next to 19 which asserts the opposite for $strobe. Bonus defect this rewrite closes: 11.6.16's `-> sys func type -- int: vpiSysFuncType` has no fixture anywhere in the chapter that calls a VALUED system function -- 06 and 20 are rejects and 19's $strobe is valueless -- so the chapter's only sys-func-call objects have neither a value nor a type. `//! temp` is a real directive (15 fixtures use it) and $temperature appears in 11 fixtures tree-wide, so a real-valued LRM-defined system function is available here at no cost.
expected: Rewrite runnable so it pins the sys-func-call object that DOES have a value and a type: `//! lrm 11.6.16`, `//! lrm 9.10`, `//! temp 300.15`, `//! bias V(p) = 1.5, V(n) = 0.25`, then `CHECKX("$temperature is a real-valued system function (9.10)", $temperature, 300.15)` -- a compiler that types the call integer truncates to 300 -- plus `CHECKX("and the probe alongside it", V(p,n), 1.25)` and `I(p,n) <+ V(p,n);`. Delete 20_system_function_call_object_atomic.expected-error.txt (covered by ch11-05).

title: 19's header states the suite's expectation backwards and is the prose keeping the 06/20 defect alive
detail: VERIFIED lines 14-17: 'This fixture deliberately uses an LRM-DEFINED task. The unregistered VPI spelling (`$fixture_vpi_task`) belongs to 05/08/20, which require it to be REFUSED; asserting continuation across one of those would bake the opposite expectation into the suite.' 05:29-31 does exactly that today ($fixture_vpi_task called, `CHECKI("the block continues past an unregistered system task call", seq, 3)`), and 08 does the same with $fixture_value_change_callback. So the warning describes the directory backwards, and it is the only place left that presents the reject expectation as settled -- a future author reading 19 repairs the wrong file.
expected: Replace lines 14-17 with the true distinction: '05 and 08 make the same 5.3.1 ordering claim across an UNREGISTERED $name, which 2.8.3 makes legal source; this one makes it across $strobe, which 9.4.1 defines, so it holds even for a compiler that refuses unregistered names.' Add `//! lrm 11.6.16` and `//! lrm 9.4.1` while in the file. Must land in the same commit as ch11-01/ch11-02 or it goes stale again.

title: The chapter's only two sound rejects carry no //! lrm cite, and the clause they pin is 4.7, not Clause 11
detail: VERIFIED: `grep -c '//! lrm' ch11_vpi/*.va` is 0 for all 26 files; the only directives present are bias/sweep/param/reject. Both fixtures already pin a CODE (`//! reject E0512` + a name substring), which is the preferred form per tests/fixtures/README.md, so only the cite is missing. src/diag_code.zig:1575 gives E0512 `.title = "unknown function"`, `.lrm = "4.7"` -- so 4.7 is the clause, and it is what travels to a compiler that does not emit E0512. Clause 11 cannot be cited by any reject in this directory because it states no error rule (see ch11-08). Both files also carry a vestigial `// EXPECT: error` on line 3 from the retired sidecar contract -- a third, weaker expectation sitting next to the two `//! reject` lines.
expected: 09: add `//! lrm 4.7` and `//! lrm 11.4` (11.4 records WHY the name was chosen -- vpi_get is a Table 11-1/11-4 C routine). 10: add `//! lrm 4.7` and `//! lrm 11.2.1`. Delete the `// EXPECT: error` line from both. No `//! xfail`: VerA already emits E0512 correctly.

title: Four dead .expected-error.txt sidecars survive the retired contract and duplicate the 06/20 justification prose
detail: VERIFIED all four exist in the directory. tests/fixtures/README.md line 3: '859 .va files. One runner, tests/torture.zig. No sidecar files.' Nothing reads them; torture.zig reads only the `//!` directives in the .va. 06's and 20's sidecars carry a second copy of the 'must be refused rather than faked' justification, which must change when ch11-01/ch11-02 land -- a guaranteed drift site. 09's and 10's are a stale duplicate of their `//! reject` lines.
expected: Delete all four files. Nothing else changes; the `//! reject` lines already carry the whole expectation.

title: 02's 'flow quantity' assertion never probes a flow -- it re-checks the potential divided by a constant, and it is the contribution's own RHS
detail:
VERIFIED line 15: ``CHECKR("the flow quantity the branch carries", V(measured)/1000.0, 5.0e-4, 1e-15);`` The arithmetic is right and bit-exact (V(measured) = 0.75 - 0.25 = 0.5 exactly per 5.4.1; 0.5/1000.0 == 5.0e-4, both 0x1.0624dd2f1a9fcp-11) so the tolerance is never exercised -- but the operand is the potential again, and it is character-for-character the RHS of the contribution on line 16, so the same expression supplies both the claim and the model. 11.6.7 is precisely the clause about a branch owning BOTH a potential quantity and a flow quantity; a compiler with no flow quantity at all passes this line. Nothing in the file reads I(measured) or I(

). The suite already has the correct idiom: ch05_analog_behavior/source_probe_both.va probes V(b) and I(b) as 'two independent unknowns of the solve' at a swept operating point.
expected: Make line 15 an actual flow probe on the ch05/source_probe_both.va model: add `//! sweep flowZ28pZ2cnZ29 = 0.002` and write ``CHECKX("named branch potential is its node pair", V(measured), 0.5);`` / ``CHECKX("the branch's flow is a second, independent quantity", I(measured), 2.0e-3);`` keeping `I(measured) <+ V(measured)/1000.0;`. Add `//! lrm 11.6.7` and `//! lrm 5.4.1`. Do NOT delete 02 (a lens proposed it): 14 and 15 do not make the two-quantities-are-distinct claim on a scalar named branch this cheaply.

title: vpiFlow is a boolean the chapter can never make false: all 22 contributions are I(...) <+, and COVERAGE.md:45 claims otherwise
detail: VERIFIED. 11.6.20 gives the contribs class `-> flow -- bool: vpiFlow` (3 hits for vpiFlow, 5 for vpiDirect in the clause HTML). `grep -E 'V *\([^)]*\) *<\+' ch11_vpi/*.va` returns nothing: every contribution in the directory is `I(...) <+` (19x I(p,n), 2x I(path), 1x I(measured)). COVERAGE.md:45 nevertheless reads 's11-6-20 | Contribution and direct/flow properties: 23_contribution_object.va', and 23 holds only `I(p,n) <+ V(p,n) / 1k` -- a fixture that cannot distinguish the property it is credited with. This is the one 11.6 object with ZERO representative of either spelling in a directory whose stated purpose (COVERAGE.md:7-8, 25) is one representative source object per row. The vpiDirect half (5.6.7 `V(out) : V(pin,nin) == 0;`) is likewise absent here but IS covered tree-wide -- ch05_analog_behavior/indirect_contribution.va, multiple_indirect.va, indirect_and_direct.va, annex_a_syntax/21, exhaustive/084 -- so it gets a cross-reference in ch11-08, not a second new file.
expected: New 12-line fixture following the directory's NN_snake_case.va convention. `//! lrm 11.6.20`, `//! lrm 5.6.2`, `//! bias V(p) = 1.5, V(n) = 0.25`, then `parameter real vsrc = 1.25;` and `CHECKX("the potential source value driven onto the branch", vsrc, 1.25); CHECKX("the branch probe alongside the potential source", V(p,n), 1.25); V(p,n) <+ vsrc;`. Both literals derived by hand: vsrc is its own 3.4 default, V(p,n) = 1.5 - 0.25 = 1.25, both dyadic and exact. Update COVERAGE.md:45 to name 23 (flow) + 27 (potential) + ch05/indirect_contribution.va (vpiDirect).

title: Eleven COVERAGE rows credit scalar/single-valued fixtures with properties they cannot exercise; the honest fix is cross-references, not new fixtures
detail:
VERIFIED each claim below by grep over the directory and over the whole fixtures tree. Clause 11 defines no Verilog-AMS production, so these rows owe accurate pointers, not clones. Rows to correct: s11-6-2 nature vpiParent/vpiChild -- the directory has only stock `electrical`, but derived natures ARE covered at ch03_data_types/10_nature_declarations.va, 36_derived_nature_inheritance.va, 37, 38, 20 (the uncovered lens claimed none exist anywhere; that is false). s11-6-3 io decl vpiDirection -- 04/12/18 declare `input` only; output/inout are covered at ch04_expressions/39_function_output_inout.va. s11-6-4/6-5/6-6 vpiScalar/vpiVector/vpiSize/vpiLeftRange/vpiPosNode/vpiNegNode -- every port, node and branch in all 26 files is scalar (no `electrical [` and no bit-select anywhere); vector nets are covered at ch03_data_types/32_vector_nets.va and ch05/vector_access.va, vector BRANCHES are open VerA debt already snapshotted at ch03_data_types/33_vector_branches.va (`//! reject DiagnosticsReported` under a DEBT header), a ground-defaulted single-terminal branch is at ch05/single_terminal_branch.va and ch03/14_named_branches.va, and the port branch `branch (

)` is snapshotted at ch03/22_port_branch_rejected.va. s11-6-10 vpiArray/var select -- 16 has scalars only; real arrays are covered in 11 fixtures tree-wide. s11-6-12 vpiConstType -- only `parameter real` here; ch03/04_parameter_types.va and 05_parameter_ranges.va have the rest. s11-6-19 `analog oper` -- zero analog operators in all 26 files (no ddt/idt/transition/slew/absdelay/laplace/limexp/white_noise/last_crossing); 4.5.3's 'In DC analysis, ddt() returns zero (0)' is already pinned verbatim at ch04_expressions/14_ddt.va:24, so cite it. s11-6-20 -- see ch11-07. s11-6-22 while/repeat -- 07 and 25 use `for` only; while is in 5 fixtures and repeat in 4 tree-wide. s11-6-23 vpiCaseType -- only vpiCase is reachable: Annex C states verbatim 'casex and casez are not supported in Verilog-A', and the rejections live at annex_c_analog_subset/11_casex_rejected.va and 12_casez_rejected.va. Two findings also belong in the header prose: (a) Clause 11 contains ZERO source-language prohibitions -- counted on the stripped HTML: 'shall be an error' 0, 'illegal' 0, 'is an error' 0, 'not permitted' 0, 'must not' 0, 'may not' 0, 'not allowed' 0, 'prohibited' 0, 'cannot' 0; the 4 'shall not' are 11.5.1 diagram legend and 11.6.4 NOTE 3/4 and 11.6.25 NOTE 5, all C-object-model -- so the absence of negatives here is a result, not a gap; (b) 11.6.10's NOTE 'vpiLeftRange and vpiRightRange shall be invalid for reals, since there can not be arrays of reals' is a 1364-2001 carryover contradicted inside the same standard by 3.2 (`real gain_factor[1:30];`, `real vtable[0:16][0:7][0:64];`) and 3.4.4/3.4.8 -- record it as deliberately NOT tested so the next author does not build `//! reject` on `real a[0:3];` and reject legal Verilog-AMS.
expected: One pass over COVERAGE.md: retarget the eleven rows above to the fixtures that actually exercise them, add the zero-prohibitions sentence and the 11.6.10 trap note to the header prose, and add 27_potential_contribution_object.va to the literal fixture inventory. No new .va files from this item.

detail: VERIFIED. 11.6.2 gives both discipline and nature a one-to-many relationship to param assign, and the only Verilog-AMS spelling that reads one is 5.5.3's `net_identifier.potential_or_flow.nature_attribute_identifier` (Syntax 5-4). The single fixture in the whole tree using it is `//! reject expected \`)\`` with `// EXPECT: error -- net.potential.abstol is not represented by the AST` -- i.e. it pins VerA's PARSER failing on construct 5.5.3 makes legal, with no `//! lrm`, no `//! xfail`, and a reject substring that is a bare parser-expectation string. title: 11.6.23 NOTE 1 -- 'the case item shall group all case conditions which branch to the same statement' -- has no multi-condition item anywhere in the chapter
detail: VERIFIED in the clause HTML: 'NOTES 1--The case item shall group all case conditions which branch to the same statement.' That one-to-many edge from case item to expr is the whole content of the NOTE. The chapter's two case statements are 07 (`3:`, `default:`) and 26:17-20 (`1:`, `default:`) -- every item has exactly one expression, so the relationship is never more than one-to-one. 5.8.3's grammar is `analog_expression { , analog_expression } : analog_statement_or_null`. Covered tree-wide (ch05/case_statement.va, annex_a_syntax/05, exhaustive/103) but this is a three-line edit to the fixture the row already names, and it is the exact NOTE.

Keep the existing 0.25 assertion; add `CHECKX("a case item groups several conditions onto one statement (11.6.23 NOTE 1)", result2, 1.25)`. Add `//! lrm 11.6.23` and `//! lrm 5.8.3`.

title: Twelve assertions use a 1e-15 tolerance on values whose own header comments claim bit-exactness, while twenty CHECKX in the same directory bet the other way
detail: VERIFIED by grep -- 12 sites, both lenses undercounted (7 and 10) and both missed 14_branch_object.va:15 and :16: 01:15 (0.5), 02:14 (0.5), 02:15 CHECKR (5.0e-4), 03:21 (2.5), 07:27 (5.5), 11:16 (0.5), 11:17 (-0.5), 13:16 (0.5), 13:17 (0.75), 14:15 (0.75), 14:16 CHECKR (7.5e-4), 15:22 (0.75). Directory tally: 12 CHECK, 2 CHECKR, 7 CHECKI, 20 CHECKX. Every bias here is a dyadic rational (0.125/0.25/0.5/0.625/0.75/0.875/1.5) and every operation is +, -, * or /1000 on them, so each result is exact in IEEE double. 1e-15 absolute against 0.5 is about 9 ulp (ulp = 1.11e-16 across [0.5,1)); CHECKR 1e-15 is about 4.5 ulp. 08:26 already proves the point in this directory at the identical bias: ``CHECKX("and the probe is unchanged by it", V(p,n), 0.5)`` with the header 'both bias values are exact in binary, so exact equality is the right strength'. Cosmetic today -- the assertion is simply 9 ulp weaker than the sentence written above it.
expected: Author's choice, one way for the whole class: promote each of the twelve to CHECKX with the same digits (0.5, 0.5, 5.0e-4, 2.5, 5.5, 0.5, -0.5, 0.5, 0.75, 0.75, 7.5e-4, 0.75), or delete the 'exact in binary / to the last bit' sentence from those headers so no file claims more than it checks. Do not do half.
